Hi, Enzo

Try looking for RRO in the following path:

/Library/Frameworks/

I hope this helps.

PS. I have also responded to your cross-post on Stack Overflow (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26494145/issues-with-revolution-r-open-yosemite-sublime-text) and created a [rro] tag.

Andrie


On Tuesday, October 21, 2014 7:30:17 PM UTC+1, Enzo wrote:
I have tried to install RRO on a new macbook pro 13" retina (two cores) & Yosemite.

I tried with RSTUDIO and R 25 (S. Urbinek notorious benchmark) and I got the test time down from ~30 s to a blazing 5 s.  Marvellous!

The problems are with Sublime text.  I use sublime text as text console more often than rstudio for a variety of reasons.

I use it with the package R-Box driving where I want to send the code to: either to the R console, or with SublimeREPL R to sublime itself splitting the screen and sending the code to the right hand of the screen where I run the R console.

Normally I configure R-Box user settings specifying just R,  and SublimeREPL specifying the R path as /usr/bin/R.  

Results (sadly)
R-Box & R does not work:  it cannot find the RRO app (even changing the name to R it does not find it).

R-Box & SublimeREPL (i.e. the console in the right side of the screen) shows the console OK, but not the prompt, hence it is of no use.

Unfortunately for me it is really important to have the above two ways of working available.

Let me know if you need the Sublime Text user scripts (also documented in a variety of places in the web).

I'll post this to stackoverflow just in case.

Any help please?

messages.subject: Re: issues with RRO + Yosemite + Sublime Text
parts:
Hacked / resolved the second problem:

Apparently SublimeREPL &  RRO  wants a setting of "echo = true" for Sublime text, but in the file at ~/Library/Application Support/Sublime Text 3/Packages/SublimeREPL/config/R is set to false. Change it to true resolve the second problem and the R prompt becomes visible.  Not sure how to set it from the Sublime console though.

@Andrie, R is visible at the OSX console thanks to a sym lynk to /Library/Framework etc., so the problem is elsewhere.  Thanks for the RRO tags on stackoverflow!

messages.subject: Re: issues with RRO + Yosemite + Sublime Text
parts:
Resolved (sort of).

The first issues with R-Box is resolved changing RRO app name to R.app (alias didn't work and I had explicitly to change the name of the app).

As in my comment above, the second issue with SublimeREPL is resolved changing the setting  of "echo = true" in the file at ~/Library/Application Support/Sublime Text 3/Packages/SublimeREPL/config/R (otherwise set to false).

As the change it is not in a file "customisable" in the console one needs to probably change it at any new release of SublimeREPL.

It remains a mystery to me why R works fine with echo=false and RRO requires echo=true.

messages.subject: Re: issues with RRO + Yosemite + Sublime Text
parts:
Well, first of all, what are you trying to achieve?  Have you succeeded in using these feature with standard R?

Beyond having all this into the code, with either R or RRO you have to :
a) split the screen in two with View>Layout>2 columns
b) call the "command palette" with <shift><p><cmd>
c) select SublimeREPL:R

At this stage you should see in one of the two half of the Sublime screen the R prompt signalling that your R console is not part of Sublime.

As I have changed also line 26 (see below), I only see the prompt (no verbose introduction to the R version etc.).

                            "osx": ["R", "--quiet", "--vanilla"],


And, most important of all, it is how to send the code to the console.  If you have R-box installed, the command to execute a number of lines previously selected with <control><a>  will be <cmd><enter>.

Hope it helps.
